Stage 1 saw only the Lean declarations and their definitions (no manuscript, no
project history). Stage 2 saw only the stage 1 read-back and the contract.

## Stage 1 -- read-back (fresh agent, Lean only)

> `congCogenerated_iInter_le Sig A (L : ι → Sub A.1) : sortedEqvLe
> (sortedEqv_iInf (fun j => congCogenerated Sig A (L j)))
> (congCogenerated Sig A (fun s => ⋂ j, L j s))`. `sortedEqv_iInf` is the
> componentwise meet; `⋂ j, L j s` is the per-sort intersection; no `Nonempty ι`
> hypothesis is present (an empty index makes both sides universal).
> Proof: (`hchar`) each `Ω^A(L^j) ⊆ Ker(ch^{L^j})` by `B-P022`(2), hence the meet
> is contained in `Ker(ch^{⋂ L^j})`; (`hcong`) the meet of congruences is a
> congruence; then `B-P022`(3) gives the refinement.

## Stage 2 -- comparison (fresh agent, read-back + contract only)

> **Outcome: formal_stronger.**
>
> Left side is `⋂_j Ω^A(L^j)`, right side `Ω^A(⋂_j L^j)`, order is pointwise
> refinement — all match. The only delta is that the Lean drops the contract's
> nonemptiness of `J`: on the empty index both sides are the universal relation,
> so the empty case is true and the statement is a faithful conservative
> generalization. No hypothesis added; no size mismatch; the proof does not
> secretly use nonemptiness.
